comments.author: Sam Tobin-Hochstadt
comments.markdown: This is a wonderful post. If I may offer a small suggestion, the claim “you must be much smarter than I am if you don’t need types” is not a good thing to say, because it never comes across as sincere.

comments.author: Alex Goodfriend
comments.markdown:
“The only thing you need category theory for is to take great categorical and mathematical concepts from the world and import them back to programming, and translate them along the way so that others don’t need to make the same journey you did.”

Hi, I’m a young Haskell enthusiast, and I want to do exactly this. I’d love some advice if anyone has any. I just finished my MS in applied math but have no large-scale software development experience, so I’m wondering where to start, and what might help (eventually) land a job I actually enjoy. GHC (and what part, if so)? A smaller project/library? Any thoughts?

comments.author: mk12
comments.markdown: A long time ago on a Haskell IRC, I asked about argument passing in Haskell and whether an array would be passed as a pointer, or copied. I was told I had a “strange mental model” by a helpful snob.
